method: Notes are read as scientific pitch notation, with middle C at C4 and A4 at the 440 Hz reference, so a note's MIDI number is (octave + 1) x 12 plus its pitch class and accidental, and inputs are limited to C0 to B8. A transposition shifts every note of the melody by the same number of semitones, so the melody keeps its shape and the interval between its lowest and highest note never changes; the page tests shifts of -12 to +12 semitones. A shift counts as a fit only when the transposed lowest note is at or above the voice's lowest comfortable note and the transposed highest note is at or below the voice's highest comfortable note, which is equivalent to the closed window from voice low minus melody low to voice high minus melody high. When the melody already fits at a shift of zero that is the recommendation, because a song that fits is normally left in its key; otherwise the recommended shift is the fitting one whose smaller end margin, min(melody low minus voice low, voice high minus melody high), is largest, which puts the melody as near the middle of the voice as the search allows, with the smaller absolute shift breaking a tie. When no shift fits, because the melody is wider than the voice, the page says so and lists the three shifts that leave the fewest semitones outside the voice, counting an overflowing note once per semitone it misses by. The key you would sing in is the starting key moved by the same number of semitones, named from the conventional twelve spellings of the major mode (C, Db, D, Eb, E, F, F#, G, Ab, A, Bb, B) and of the natural minor mode (C, C#, D, Eb, E, F, F#, G, G#, A, Bb, B), and transposed melody notes are spelled with flats when the new key's name carries a flat and with sharps otherwise. Tessitura, stamina, passaggio, breath, ornamentation, voice leading and any Fach classification are not modelled, so the result is a range comparison rather than a decision. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Transposition (music): transposition moves a collection of notes up or down by a constant interval, chromatic transposition shifts every pitch by the same number of semitones, and singers ask for a different key to fit their vocal range
Wikipedia, Scientific pitch notation: middle C is C4, the octave number rises from B to C, A4 is 440 Hz under the current standard, and a MIDI note m has frequency 440 x 2^((m - 69)/12) Hz

Conventional key names: the twelve major keys are C, Db, D, Eb, E, F, F#, G, Ab, A, Bb and B, and the twelve natural minor keys C, C#, D, Eb, E, F, F#, G, G#, A, Bb and B, each spelled with the fewest accidentals
